Summary:
The provided “data source” consists solely of the bibliography section of an academic paper (nineteen numbered references) with no narrative text, abstract, methods, findings, discussion, or conclusions.  Because it is only a list of citations, it contains:
1. No explicit statements of AI-related risks or problems.
2. No articulated causal chains, theoretical insights, or design rationales.
3. No descriptions of implementation mechanisms, validation evidence, or proposed interventions.

Hence, the mandatory criteria requiring extraction of “complete causal-interventional pathways … from risks/problems → methods → findings → proposed interventions” cannot be met.  Any attempt to fabricate nodes or edges would rely entirely on speculation that is not present in the source text and would violate the instruction against inventing unsupported content.

Inference strategy justification:
• The prompt allows “moderate inference” only to bridge gaps between clearly present concepts. Here, there are no source concepts at all—only isolated reference titles. Creating pathways would require strong speculation (confidence level 1) for every element, which would produce an ungrounded and misleading fabric.  
• Therefore, the correct action is to declare the extraction impossible and provide a detailed explanation so the overall pipeline can improve its handling of purely bibliographic inputs.

Extraction completeness explanation:
• All content was reviewed.  No extractable claims exist.  
• Supplying an empty node/edge set is thus complete and faithful.

Key limitations:
• Bibliography-only inputs should be detected upstream and either discarded or paired with the body text.
• Current instructions might add a pre-check step: “If source contains <300 contiguous non-reference words of prose, abort extraction and flag.”

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[95]

```json
{
  "nodes": [],
  "edges": []
}
```
